title: Embedding Prior Task-specific Knowledge into Language Models for Context-aware Document Ranking

problem.claim: Context-aware document ranking should exploit users' contextual behaviors in the current session.

gap.claim: Fine-tuning pre-trained language models on noisy search logs may prevent them from fully mastering effective context-aware search knowledge.

contributions.claim: LOCK explicitly embeds task-specific prior knowledge into pre-trained language models to guide optimization for context-aware document ranking.
LOCK identifies intra-turn, inter-turn, and global session signals and formulates them as prior attention biases.
LOCK adds task-specific pre-training using masked language modeling and soft reconstruction of the prior attention matrix.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments validate the effectiveness and convergence of LOCK.

narrative_sequence.summary: Contextual behaviors in the current session are favorable for document ranking, and pre-trained language models have benefited the task.
Existing models implicitly learn task-specific knowledge from noisy search logs, which may limit their mastery of effective search knowledge.
The authors propose LOCK, which explicitly embeds task-specific prior knowledge into pre-trained language models.
LOCK uses three levels of session signals as prior attention biases and adds task-specific pre-training.
The authors report improved convergence and ranking ability, with extensive experiments validating effectiveness and convergence.

source_observation.claim: Search logs contain varied user intents and search patterns, creating a noisy basis for implicitly learned task-specific knowledge.

interpretation.claim: Making task-specific knowledge explicit may help guide model optimization in context-aware ranking.

application.claim: For related ranking systems, represent task-relevant session signals explicitly and incorporate them into model attention or optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported context-aware document ranking setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not detail how intra-turn, inter-turn, and global session signals are constructed.
The abstract does not report the scope of the experiments or computational costs.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported effectiveness or convergence.
